text: Morgan's Canon (C. Lloyd Morgan, 1894) is best characterized as which kind of principle?
choices: A principle of parsimony: do not interpret an animal's behavior in terms of a higher psychological faculty if a lower one will suffice
A metaphysical thesis that non-human animals never have any conscious experiences
A methodological rule to attribute the richest possible mental life to animals by default
The behaviorist claim that all behavior is exhaustively explained by stimulus-response conditioning
explanation: Morgan's Canon is a parsimony rule about interpreting behavior at the lowest adequate psychological level; crucially it does not forbid higher attributions, only requires that evidence warrant them. The second overreads it into a denial of consciousness; the third is its opposite (anthropomorphic liberality); the fourth is Watson/Skinner behaviorism.
